ego.name: Phillis Wheatley
ego.summary: Phillis Wheatley was a West African-born American poet who was enslaved in Boston and educated by the Wheatley family. Her 1773 collection Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral made her the first African-American author to publish a book of poetry.

category_summaries.summary: Wheatley’s earliest relationships formed in the Boston household that enslaved her. Mary and Nathaniel Wheatley taught her to read and write. The household gave her access to Scripture and classical literature. John and Susanna Wheatley held her in slavery until they manumitted her in November 1773.
After emancipation, Wheatley married John Peters. Their household lived in poor conditions. Peters was imprisoned for debt in 1784. Wheatley sought work while caring for an infant son.

Wheatley’s publishing circle linked Boston scrutiny to London print. Boston men signed an attestation of her authorship in 1772. Archibald Bell published her collection in London in 1773 with support from Selina Hastings. George Washington answered her poem, and Scipio Moorhead received a poem in the same collection.

Christian networks gave Wheatley routes to publication and correspondence. Selina Hastings supported her London volume. Wheatley wrote to Samson Occom about natural-born rights for enslaved people. She also exchanged letters with John Thornton about poetry and personal concerns.
